core.title: Write the artifact reference URN as the reference prefix followed by the artifact name, copied verbatim
core.given: A reference URN for an artifact appears anywhere it is authored or checked (e.g. a plan artifact, acceptance test, schema, doc, config or source file), whether new or already existing
core.when: that reference URN is written, edited, or validated
core.then: The URN is exactly the artifact's URN shape from the profile — the literal reference prefix followed immediately by the artifact name copied verbatim — preserving every separator character (colon and dot) exactly as written.
prefer: Copy the artifact name as-is after the reference prefix, so the URN is the prefix followed by the exact, unchanged name.
Keep multi-segment artifact names intact, including every separator, when writing the reference URN.
avoid: Normalising separators (turning colons into dots or slashes, or dots into colons) inside the URN.
Shortening, re-casing, dropping or adding segments so the URN no longer equals the artifact name.
Inventing a reference-URN form other than the profile's artifact URN shape (reference prefix plus artifact name).
core.why: The reference URN is the URN form of the artifact name; an exact mirror keeps one artifact identity that references and the artifact's schema identifier can share without translation.
evidence: For every reference URN found (new or pre-existing, in any location), stripping the reference prefix yields a string identical to the referenced artifact name (the artifact need not already exist; planned artifacts count).
verification: The check compares by exact string equality: the text after the literal reference prefix must equal the referenced artifact name, with every separator character (colon, dot) significant and unnormalised.
The check does not require the referenced artifact to already exist; planned artifacts count.

Scan scope is not limited to plan artifacts or to changed lines: every reference URN is validated wherever it occurs in authored or checked repository text (plan artifacts, tests, docs, schemas, config and code).
A change-level view (a reference URN added or edited in the diff) is one trigger among several, not a gate; validation is not limited to it.

The reference-URN shape (prefix plus artifact name) is instantiated from the profile's artifact URN shape; the rule's own term, detector and finding ids are realization details of the stack realization.

values: reference-URN token present in any repository text (new, edited or pre-existing)

fires: Any document or file (e.g. an acceptance artifact, plan artifact, schema or config) writes the reference URN for an artifact.
A plan artifact lists produced/consumed artifacts with their reference URNs.
An artifact is renamed and the reference URNs that point at it must be updated.
A review or validation pass checks existing reference URNs that were not edited in the current change.
doesNotFire: Text names an artifact without writing or checking any reference URN.
Deciding the artifact name itself (governed by planner.artifact-naming.naming-pattern).

profileRequirements.meaning: The URN shape by which an artifact (component) is referenced — a literal reference prefix followed by the artifact name. The core obligates the text after that prefix to be the artifact name copied verbatim, separators preserved.

bunOnly.text: Source examples hold: commons:identifiers.uuid -> contract:commons:identifiers.uuid; commons:ux:foundations:color.primary -> contract:commons:ux:foundations:color.primary.
bunOnly.reason: Concrete worked examples of the Bun realization; bun.json itself is delivered as the reference example, so the core does not repeat them.

bunOnly.text: Term contract_urn: the URN form of an artifact name; pattern contract:{artifact_name}.
bunOnly.reason: The term id of this rule is a realization detail (not a profile key, not core); the pattern itself is carried by the core through the profile's artifact URN shape.

classification.note: Stack artifact kinds in the example list (plan, product capability, DESIRED OUTCOME, acceptance) generalised to plan artifact / source file / acceptance test; the reference-URN concept instantiates from urn.component.
The concrete shape 'contract:{artifact_name}' is the profile's artifact URN shape; the core keeps the verbatim-copy obligation and separator preservation.
'schema $id' generalised to 'schema identifier'; the single-shared-identity rationale is neutral.
Guidance kept; the concrete commons:identifiers.uuid example is not repeated in the core (bun.json is the reference example).
Multi-segment guidance kept; the concrete example is not repeated in the core.
'A URN form other than contract:{artifact_name}' becomes 'other than the profile's artifact URN shape'.
'contract:*' becomes reference URNs with the prefix from the profile; the no-existence requirement (planned artifacts count) is kept.
Concrete worked examples; the core does not repeat them.
The definition (reference URN = prefix + artifact name) goes to verification with the shape from the profile; the term id contract_urn is a realization detail.
Exact string equality, separator significance and the no-existence requirement go to verification.
Unrestricted scan scope (not only plan artifacts, not only changed lines) goes to verification.
Task terms kept; the literal prefix token 'contract:' instantiates from the artifact URN shape.

Finding fact kept as needs_new_observer; the detector's everywhere-scope (plans, product capabilities, DESIRED OUTCOMES, acceptances, docs, schemas, code, config in the Bun text) is reflected generically in verification.
Change fact kept as needs_new_observer; 'one trigger among several, not a gate' is reflected in verification.

neutralityNotes: The literal reference prefix and pattern 'contract:{artifact_name}' are per-stack data carried by the existing profile key urn.component; the core speaks of the 'reference URN' as the reference prefix plus the artifact name copied verbatim (Bun's local term is 'contract URN'). Stack artifact kinds in examples (product capability, DESIRED OUTCOME, plan doc) were generalised to plan artifact / source file / acceptance test. 'schema $id' was generalised to 'schema identifier'. Sibling rule ids in doesNotFire (planner.artifact-naming.naming-pattern, planner.artifact-naming.schema-identifier) were kept verbatim: they are method-level ids, assumed stable across realizations since this rule's own id maps 1:1 in rule.json. Concrete worked examples and the rule's term id remain only in bun.json (bunOnly).
